architecture.mechanism: Sulphite content in consumed alcohol influences driver lateral vehicle control and cognitive performance under demanding urban driving environments.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a real-time cabin air chemical sensor and driver biometric feedback loop into the high-performance car's ADAS to detect elevated environmental toxins (analogs of sulphites) or driver physiological impairment, dynamically limiting top speed and reducing power to enforce road-legal safe driving parameters.
architecture.expected_effect: The vehicle autonomously restricts performance capabilities (speed/torque) when driver impairment or toxic exposure is detected, preventing loss of lateral control and ensuring adherence to road legal engineering limits.
architecture.falsification_test: Simulate driving in a demanding urban environment with elevated ambient chemical triggers while measuring lateral deviation and top speed; if the vehicle fails to cap speed or maintain lane discipline within legal thresholds despite sensor input, the intervention fails.
